# Chapter 2: The Tribune's Gambit

**Applying Guy Sclanders' Methodology**

## Session Overview

A Tribune arrives from Rome with sealed Senate orders regarding the spear. That night, Germanic raiders attack in force — with suspicious timing. The party must defend the fort, expose the Tribune's real agenda, and decide what to do with a man who might be right for all the wrong reasons.

**Level:** 4 → Advance to 5 at session end
**Duration:** 3–4 hours
**Key Goal:** Discover who the Tribune really serves — and whether to trust him
**Theme:** Loyalty vs. Survival (first test)

### Guy Sclanders' Principles Applied

**Pressure Cooker:** Tribune's authority creates a new power dynamic before the party has recovered from Session 1. The raid removes the option to think carefully.

**OGAS Integration:** Tribune, Legate, Vercingetorix, and Varro all have clear competing goals this session.

**Three Clue Rule:** Three independent paths to discovering Tribune Lucius is working for Brutus. Party only needs to find one.

## Scene 0: Cold Open (5 minutes)

**Start in media res — the moment before everything gets worse.**

The morning BEFORE the Tribune arrives. Dawn watch. One of the fort's gate sentries has been found dead — throat cut, no struggle, no tracks. Carved into the wooden palisade beside him, deep and deliberate:

**ROMA CADIT.** *(Rome falls.)*

**Read aloud (slowly):**

> *Dawn. Someone is shaking you awake before the trumpet sounds.*
>
> *Outside, a cluster of soldiers stands at the north gate. At their feet, Sextus — the sentry you spoke to last night, the one with the bad knee who always complained about the cold — lies with his throat open and his eyes still surprised. No tracks. No blood trail. No explanation.*
>
> *Centurion Varro crouches beside the body. He looks up at you. His voice is very quiet:*
>
> *"This was done by someone who knew his patrol route. Someone inside the walls."*
>
> *He points to the carving in the wood.*
>
> *Before anyone can speak, a trumpet call from the far side of the fort: three long notes, the signal for visitors on the road.*
>
> *Through the south gate, riders in gleaming armor approach.*

**DM Direction:** Don't let them investigate the sentry's death now. The world has immediately moved on. They're holding an unsolved murder in their hands while an entirely new crisis walks through the gate.


## Road Encounters (d8)

The journey from Vindolanda north toward the chieftain's territory takes the better part of a day on the frontier road. Run 2–3 of these encounters, choosing or rolling randomly. Each is a 5–10 minute scene. They seed the session's themes, give scouts and naturalists something to do, and accumulate evidence the party can connect later.

| d8 | Encounter |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Abandoned Shrine** — A roadside Lararium, three dead travelers around it, hands pressed to the stone as if they died praying. Freshly killed within 24 hours. No wounds. Investigation DC 13: faint scorch-marks on the stone, matching the vault's corruption signature. Someone is using sacred sites for something other than worship. |
| 2 | **Shadow Stalkers** — Two Shadows from the vault have followed the spear (or whoever touched it last). They do not attack in daylight. At the first dusk camp they manifest. Perception DC 14 to notice them watching from the treeline before they commit. Placing the spear on the ground and covering it for the night makes them retreat. |
| 3 | **Watching Eyes** — A Germanic warrior sits in a tree twenty feet off the road, making no effort to hide. If acknowledged by gesture — Insight DC 11 to read this as a test, not a threat — he drops down, walks past without speaking, and disappears into the forest. Vercingetorix's scouts are assessing the party's temperament. How the party responds here is noted. |
| 4 | **Deserters** — Three Roman soldiers on the road moving fast, cloaks over their armor. They halt when they see the party. Not aggressive: frightened. They fled during the Session 2 raid. Persuasion DC 13 calms them; Intimidation DC 14 gets specific intel: they overheard the Tribune arguing with someone in Latin after the raid — *"This isn't what we agreed."* They can be sent back to the fort, released, or used as extra hands. |
| 5 | **Ambushed Rider** — A military courier's horse stands alone on the road, rider missing. Saddlebags torn and scattered. Investigation DC 13: the rider's footprints lead into the forest, but the ambushers left no tracks — Survival DC 15 confirms this is impossible for any group. Survival DC 11: the rider was dragged backward, not chased. Scattered papers include a supply request sealed with a wax mark matching Handout 5's Senate correspondence. Someone is intercepting dispatches before they reach the fort. |
| 6 | **Roadside Cultists** — Four Cult of Mars Initiates performing a ritual at a stone milestone, burning offerings and chanting. They scatter on sight. Investigation DC 12 at the ritual site: fresh blood, a carved OTHALAN rune burned into the stone, a clay soldier-figure with a pin through the head. Haruspex/Religion DC 13: this is an active curse rite targeting a specific person. The figure's crude armor marks it as optio-rank — potentially someone in the party's unit. |
| 7 | **Swarm of Ravens** — Three hundred ravens fill the sky for one full round, all silent, in a column formation, then wheel north and vanish. Haruspex/Religion DC 12: a flock that moves like a marching column is directed attention, not natural behavior. The direction they turned is the direction the party is heading. Nature DC 13: there are at least three corvid species in that formation. Ravens do not flock with other species. Something is driving them. |
| 8 | **Waylaid Convoy** — Two *vicus* traders from Vindolanda are on the road, cart blocked by a fallen tree. They are relieved to see the party. The older trader mentions that Aldric — *"the quiet scholar above the taberna, buys strange plants"* — paid him to carry a sealed message north last week. He doesn't know who received it. He just knows he felt wrong about it afterward and wished he hadn't taken the coin. He doesn't know what was in the message. He is just an ordinary man who made 3 *denarii* and has been uncomfortable since. |


## The Sextus Murder: A Three Clue Rule Mystery

The dead sentry is not a dropped thread. It's the first evidence of Brutus' reach -- he has a sleeper agent inside the fort. The agent (Decanus Quintus Flavius, a 12-year veteran who owes his family's debts to a man connected to Brutus) killed Sextus when Sextus caught him tampering with the spear's storage chains the night before. He then carved "ROMA CADIT" as misdirection -- making it look like a Germanic or dissident act -- and left the fort with the Tribune's entourage, hiding in plain sight.

**Timeline note:** Quintus Flavius was pre-arranged by Brutus to join the Tribune's escort weeks in advance as a "local liaison" -- the paperwork was prepared before the Tribune's arrival and delivered with the sealed orders. The Tribune may not know who Quintus actually is. Quintus killed Sextus that specific morning because he knew it was his last opportunity before the Tribune's departure began the following day. The timing was his. The cover was Brutus'.

The party doesn't need to solve this in Session 2. But the clues are here.

**Clue 1: The Wound**

Perception DC 11 (active: reading the body's position before touching anything): Sextus is facing the wall he was supposed to be watching. He did not turn toward the threat. He was walking away from someone he had already assessed as not dangerous. He let the attacker close without raising an arm. This is not a soldier caught by surprise from behind -- it is a soldier who did not read another soldier as a threat until it was too late. He knew the person who killed him.

Medicine DC 13 (active: examining the body):

- The cut is precise. One stroke, left-to-right, from behind. Sextus had no defensive wounds.
- Someone who knew exactly where to stand and how to move. This is trained work, not rage.
- The blade angle indicates a right-handed attacker shorter than Sextus -- and Sextus was short.

**Clue 2: The Boot Print**

Investigation DC 14 (active: examining the ground near the carving) or Survival DC 12 (active: reading the ground first before looking at the message):

- Investigation: One clear boot print in the mud below the carved message. Legionary-issue hobnail, size small, but the wear pattern is unusual: the inside heel is heavily worn, indicating a man who turns his foot slightly when he walks.
- Survival alternative: The character reads the approach path first -- the carver came from inside the fort, not from the gate, and left toward the stables. The boot print is confirmation, not the starting point.
- If the party has a chance to observe the Tribune's entourage before they leave: Decanus Quintus walks exactly like this. Perception DC 15 (active: watching the departure specifically) to notice it.

**Clue 3: Varro Knows Something**

If the party asks Varro directly about Sextus:

> *"Sextus had the north gate rotation memorized to the hour. Anyone who wanted to know when he'd be alone had three options: bribe him -- which didn't work, I knew him -- watch the rotation board -- which is in the principia -- or ask someone who knew the schedule. There are forty men who know that schedule."*

If the party asks whether anyone left with the Tribune: *"One man asked for transfer papers this morning. Fast. I've been trying to remember his name. Quintus something. Twelve-year man. Quiet."* This is as far as Varro goes -- he doesn't have proof, just a feeling.


## Scene 1: The Tribune Arrives

**Tribune Lucius Valerius Maximus** enters the fort like he owns it. Young — too young for how polished he is. Rings on every finger. A cloak trimmed with purple. Six Praetorian Guards at his back, sitting their horses like statues of iron.

He surveys the fort the way a merchant surveys damaged goods.

Perception DC 12 (active: reading the Praetorian escort formation as they ride in): Six Praetorians riding in two files of three, not the standard paired escort. The lead pair's hands are on weapon hilts, not reins. The rear pair has stayed slightly apart from the center, maintaining clear strike lanes. This is a formation ready to act on a signal, not a ceremonial honor guard. The Tribune brought soldiers expecting to use them.

**Read aloud:**

> "Fort Vindolanda." He says the name as if tasting something mildly unpleasant. "Smaller than I expected. And considerably less tidy."
>
> He dismounts without waiting for assistance, hands his reins to a Praetorian, and strides toward the principia without being escorted. The Praetorians fall in around him like a moving wall.
>
> "I'll need the artifact secured in my quarters by the second hour. I'll need the Legate removed from command by the third. And I'll need whoever is responsible for this" — he gestures at the fort in general — "to explain to me why it took three days for Rome to hear about a divine weapon being unearthed on my frontier."
>
> He stops and looks at the party directly for the first time.
>
> "You must be the ones who retrieved it. Good. You're promoted. You work for me now."

**Tribune's Official Orders:**
- He carries sealed Senate orders (Handout 4 — real and legitimate)
- The spear is to be delivered to Rome immediately
- The Legate is relieved of command pending investigation
- The party is designated "Special Envoys of the Senate" — higher authority than the Legate within this fort

**Immediate NPC Reactions:**
- **Legate Corvinus**: Controlled fury. Accepts the orders publicly, seething privately. He will be a problem later.
- **Augur Cassia**: Visible distress. Whispers to the party at the first opportunity: *"The omens around this man are confused. I cannot see his purpose clearly."*
- **Centurion Varro** (quietly, to the party, when Tribune is out of earshot): *"I've seen ambitious men from Rome before. That one is afraid of something. Afraid men do stupid things."*
- Religion DC 13 (passive: noticing something off during the Tribune's formal invocations to the Senate's divine mandate): He skips the traditional ward gesture used when swearing on official authority before witnesses. A character with Religion DC 13 passive notices the omission. He either does not know the form, or he chose not to perform it. Neither option says anything good.
- Arcana DC 13 (passive: examining the ROMA CADIT carving shortly after it is found): The letter strokes are angular and deliberate -- the same runic carving technique used on the spear. Whoever made this had exposure to Germanic inscriptional practice, not Roman. A Roman carving a Latin message would use rounded, cursive strokes. These are not.


## Three Clue Rule: Discovering the Tribune's True Agenda

The party needs to learn that Lucius is working for Senator Brutus and his goal is to prevent the spear reaching Rome (not to retrieve it). Three independent paths — finding any one is enough.

**Clue 1: The Encoded Letter**
- Access Tribune's quarters: Stealth DC 13 (active: slipping past the Praetorian guard) or Deception DC 14 (active: claiming authorization for a security inventory -- if convincing, the guard gives them 10 minutes unattended)
- Inside: Investigation DC 16 (active: searching the room thoroughly) or Thieves' Tools DC 14 (active: picking the lock on the dispatch box directly)
- Decoded, it names Senator "G.C.B." ordering the artifact's "permanent removal"
- Cassia can identify the cipher pattern if shown it (she's seen similar Senate correspondence)

**Clue 2: The Tribune's Behaviour**
- Watch him carefully during the raid (Scene 2): Perception DC 14 (active: specifically watching the Tribune's movements during the alarm) or Insight DC 14 (active: reading his body language when the horns sound)
- The Tribune and his Praetorians take *no action* during the assault. They withdraw to the principia and secure it -- not the walls, not the gate. They're protecting the spear room, not the fort.
- Afterward: Tribune pushes to accelerate departure, citing "raider intelligence." Why the rush?
- Varro: *"Defenders defend the people. They defended the artifact. Ask yourself why."*

**Clue 3: Varro's Network**
- If the party asks Varro directly about the Tribune (no check needed):
- *"I did some asking around. That Tribune was posted to the financial investigation commission six months ago -- investigating military supply embezzlement. Guess who was embezzling? Start with which Senators have frontier contracts."*
- History DC 13 (passive): "G.C.B." points to Gaius Cassius Brutus -- known for his 'Republic' rhetoric and enormous wealth


## Scene 2: Investigation Window

The party has several hours before departure. The fort is tense; every soldier knows something political has happened.

**Talking to the Augur:**
Cassia is in the shrine, surrounded by omen tablets, looking exhausted.
> *"Three days ago I dreamed of the spear in Rome. The Capitoline ran with blood. There were cheering crowds."*

She reveals the spear's true history if the party hasn't already learned it: it was used by a mortal hero to kill a minor divine being — one of Mars' demigod sons. Mars cursed it: whoever wields it with ambition will be consumed by war.

*"The Tribune knows this. He isn't taking it to Rome — he's making sure it never arrives. Someone in Rome fears what it can do in the right hands. Or the wrong ones."*

If the party stays to talk further, Cassia mentions a practical problem, almost as an afterthought:

> *"Titus kept a supply of bog valerian. Valeriana palustris — grows in Germanic wetlands, standing water in forest clearings. I use it in the ward ritual. His supply is gone and I haven't been able to source more through the fort's traders. I have enough for one more full rite. After that the protective blessings on the standards and the principia run at half strength."*

She can sketch the plant. She knows it grows in the forest clearings north of the road the party is taking in Session 3. Finding one bunch — five stalks — requires a DC 13 Nature check in any wetland clearing. Without it, her protective rites in Session 4 provide only the base ward effects, not the full resistance against supernatural fear. With it, full capacity.

*She does not ask formally. She mentions it the way a tired professional mentions a supply problem she has learned to work around. The party can pursue it or not.*

**The Scholar in the Vicus:**

Aldric appears in the vicus as a Germanic-Latin translator and herb buyer, always polite, always slightly too interested in logistics. Road encounter 8 (or any inquiry into unusual *vicus* residents) can seed this conversation.

If the party watches him closely during a conversation:

- Insight DC 18 (active: watching him during a sustained exchange): He asks slightly too-precise questions about the party's departure direction, the spear's current location, and whether the Tribune is still in the fort. His framing is academic curiosity. The DC 18 reads the precision beneath the phrasing: these are intelligence questions structured to sound like small talk.
- Investigation DC 14 (active: searching his quarters above the taberna, with or without permission): A folded note in cipher matching Handout 5's letter-shift format, addressed to a contact in a southern city: *"Artifact remains at Vindolanda. Party departed north. Tribune unsuccessful."* Signed with a raven-claw symbol, not initials.

Confronted with evidence, Aldric does not fight. He is a professional who anticipated capture:

> *"I was paid to observe. I observed. I sent reports. I did not harm anyone in this fort."*

He will trade his entire contact chain — the raven-mark cipher key, the name of a secondary operative the party may encounter, the city where Brutus's people receive these reports — in exchange for his life and a two-hour head start. He delivers exactly what he promises and nothing more.

**If the party ignores him:** He sends one more report north before they leave. In Session 3, the chieftain's people will have received advance notice of the party's approach. Whether this is advantageous, disadvantageous, or neutral depends entirely on how the party handled the Session 2 raid and Vercingetorix specifically.

**Talking to Centurion Varro:**
> *"Twenty years. I've served twenty years. You know what I've learned? The men who sail into a fort from Rome and relieve the commanding officer — they're not solving problems. They're managing them. For someone else."*

He's positioned six of his veterans near the spear's storage room. Quietly. He doesn't explain, but if the party asks: *"Because if that Tribune tries to move it tonight without telling anyone, I want to know about it immediately."*

**Confronting the Tribune:**
He's charming and deflects with practiced skill. Insight DC 16 (active: reading him during a sustained conversation) to sense he's performing more than he's saying. If pushed hard (Persuasion DC 17, active: pressing directly and refusing to accept deflection, or evidence in hand), he drops the act slightly:
> *"Let's say, hypothetically, that some artifacts are more dangerous in Rome than outside it. Let's say someone with the ear of half the Senate has a plan for this particular artifact that does not end well for anyone living. Let's say I was sent here to prevent that, not to enable it."*

He will not name Brutus unless the party produces the decoded letter.


## Scene 3: The Raid

*That night.* The timing is not a coincidence.

Germanic raiders attack in force — and Vercingetorix the Red is leading them.

**Read aloud (alarm horns sounding):**

> *The first arrow takes a sentry off the wall before the alarm horn sounds.*
>
> *Then the drums start — Germanic war drums, deep and rhythmic, surrounding the fort on three sides. Torchlight beyond the palisade: dozens of torches, maybe hundreds.*
>
> *Centurion Varro's voice cuts through the confusion: "WALLS! ALL SOLDIERS TO THE WALLS! Where in Pluto's name are those Praetorians?"*
>
> *The Praetorians are nowhere near the walls. Through the principia window, you can see torchlight — they're inside, around the spear.*

Survival DC 12 (active: reading the drum pattern and torchlight distribution before the wall fight starts): The drums are synchronized from three directions, not echoing from one source. The torches are spaced too evenly for a mob. A character who has seen organized attacks before identifies this immediately: the three-side advance was staged from fixed positions, moved on a signal, and timed to arrive simultaneously. Someone coordinated this from inside the treeline for hours. It is not a raid. It is a demonstration.

### Encounter Structure

**Phase 1: The Walls** *(2 rounds)*
Raiders swarm with ladders and grappling hooks. The party can:
- Man the walls: melee attacks as ladders are pushed back (Athletics DC 12, active: pushing back a ladder with two or more men on it)
- Use the ballista: 2d10 piercing, requires 2 people, Dexterity DC 12 (active: aiming under pressure); Acrobatics DC 11 (active: reaching the ballista quickly via a non-standard route when the normal path is blocked)
- Direct the legionary response: Persuasion DC 13 or Intimidation DC 13 (active: holding frightened soldiers at their posts); Performance DC 13 (active: delivering a battle speech rather than an order -- soldiers respond to emotion, not just authority, same DC, different character type)
- Nature DC 11 (passive: noticing before the raid that the night birds near the treeline went silent two hours before the attack): A coordinated advance through undergrowth silences birds consistently. The raid was staged from far back and moved slowly into position. This was planned, not opportunistic. A character with Nature DC 11 passive who mentions being on watch during those hours knew something was wrong before the horn sounded.

*12 **Tribal Warriors** (waves, not all at once), 2 **Berserkers** on the ladders*

**Phase 2: The Breach** *(3 rounds)*
Raiders use a battering ram on the west gate. The wood holds for 3 rounds before giving. The party can:
- Defend the gate itself: massive melee fight at the chokepoint
- Find another way to stop the ram (fire, dropping stones, cutting the rope)
- Rally a counter-charge with Varro's veterans

*Centurion Varro fights alongside the party — use **Veteran** stat block. He's worth three normal soldiers.*

**Phase 3: Vercingetorix** *(arrival at breach)*

When the gate falls, a giant of a man steps through — red-haired, iron-armed, wearing a Germanic chieftain's torc and carrying a war spear that could skewer two men. He surveys the chaos with calm eyes.

**Read aloud:**

> *He doesn't charge. He walks.*
>
> *The fighting parts around him. Legionaries step back. He moves like a man who has walked through battlefields his entire life, which he has.*
>
> *He looks at the principia. Then he looks at you.*
>
> *In accented but clear Latin: "The God-Killer is here. I can feel it from here. I came for the God-Killer. I did not come for you."*

**Vercingetorix (use Gladiator stat block, CR 5)** — but he doesn't attack the party unless attacked first. He wants to reach the spear. His agenda: the spear killed his grandfather three generations ago. It is a sacred wound in his people's history.

**Decision Point during the fight:** How do they handle Vercingetorix?
- **Fight him directly** — very hard at level 4, winnable but costly
- **Let him reach the spear** — Cassia is horrified; the Legate uses this as evidence of treason
- **Talk to him** — DC 15 Persuasion: *"Tell me why it matters to your people and I'll listen"* — he stops fighting. This costs the party a round but opens a future alliance.


## Scene 4: The Tribune's Move

After the raid. Soldiers tend wounds. The gates are being repaired. Three raiders were captured.

The Tribune appears, immaculate as ever, with his Praetorians.

**Read aloud:**

> *"Well," he says, looking at the carnage. "That was unfortunate."*
>
> *He turns to the Praetorians: "Arrest them."*
>
> *One of his guards moves to flank the party. The Tribune's voice is flat, businesslike:*
>
> *"These soldiers conspired with the raiders. They signaled the attack timing from the walls. I have witnesses."*
>
> *From the far side of the courtyard, the Legate steps forward. His expression is unreadable.*
>
> *"I concur with the Tribune's assessment," he says.*
>
> *Centurion Varro takes a slow step to stand beside the party. His hand moves to his gladius. "Do you," he says.*

**Decision Point — the confrontation:**

| Option | How | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **Expose the Tribune** | Produce the decoded letter or Clue 2/3 evidence | Praetorians hesitate; Varro intervenes; Tribune trapped. Rolls to next session politically complicated. |
| **Fight** | Combat: Tribune + 6 Praetorians (CR 2 each) | Extremely dangerous. Victory means they're fugitives from Rome. |
| **Negotiate** | DC 16 Persuasion with at least one clue in hand | Tribune offers private deal: *"Help me destroy the spear my way and I'll make this go away."* |
| **Intimidate** | DC 15 Intimidation (active: controlled, precise demonstration that the party has already survived things the Tribune has not: vault undead, the raid, the spear's active corruption -- delivered calmly, not angrily, as a statement of fact about what happens to people who force this). Different from fighting: the message is "you cannot afford what comes next." On success, the Tribune pauses. His Praetorian hand-signal changes from "arrest" to "hold." He is calculating. He offers the private deal as above, but from a weaker position: he knows the party has leverage. On 5 above the DC: the Praetorians disengage entirely without a direct order. | Same as Negotiate outcome but the Tribune is more cautious about using the party as a tool in Session 3. He has been read correctly and he knows it. |
| **Flee with Vercingetorix** | He's still in the fort or just outside -- if the party treated him respectfully | He offers forest refuge: *"My enemy's enemy."* They're now fugitives but with a powerful Germanic ally. |
| **Surrender** | Give the spear to the Tribune | He thanks them politely. They're confined to quarters. Session 3 starts as prisoners being transported to Rome. |


## Conclusion

**Advance to Level 5**

Whatever happens, the party now knows three things: the Tribune is working for someone powerful in Rome, Vercingetorix has a legitimate grievance against the spear, and at least one of the people they've been trusting is not fully what they seem.

Seed for Session 3: wherever they end up, they're moving — deeper into the forest, or toward Rome, or as prisoners. The world is no longer containable within Fort Vindolanda.


## DM Notes

### OGAS This Session

**Tribune Lucius Valerius Maximus**
- **Objective:** Earn his father Brutus' respect by completing this mission
- **Goal (this session):** Get possession of the spear and arrange its destruction without leaving evidence of Senate involvement
- **Agenda:** Use legal authority to isolate the party, then manufacture a crisis that justifies destroying the spear
- **Secret:** He's not convinced destroying it is right. Cassia's arguments are getting through. He's doubting the mission.

**Senator Gaius Cassius Brutus (off-screen, never present)**
- **Objective:** Prevent the spear from reaching Rome where it passes beyond his control
- **Goal this session:** Get the Tribune to secure or destroy the spear; maintain deniability
- **Agenda:** Directs through Lucius. Has pre-positioned Quintus Flavius as an insurance agent. If the Tribune's approach fails, the fort's destruction is an acceptable outcome.
- **Secret:** Has a secondary ritual prepared -- a private ceremony under different auspices -- in case the Tribune fails entirely. He does not need the fort to survive; he only needs the spear to disappear.

**Vercingetorix the Red**
- **Objective:** Protect his people from Roman expansion
- **Goal (this session):** Reach the spear and either destroy it or take it back to his tribe's custody
- **Agenda:** Attack the fort while Roman authority is disrupted by the Tribune's arrival — the timing is deliberate
- **Secret:** He's been watching this fort for weeks. He knows more about the spear's history than any Roman.

### Vercingetorix: The Reluctant Alliance

If the party treats him with respect during the battle, he becomes the most important NPC of Sessions 3–4. He knows:
- Where the sacred grove is (a day's travel into the Teutoburg Forest)
- That the spear cannot be destroyed anywhere except there
- That the ritual requires a willing sacrifice — his grandfather tried and failed because the sacrifice was unwilling

He will not volunteer this information to Romans who disrespect him. He will tell them everything if they acknowledge his people's claim on this history.

**How he speaks:** Economical. Poetic when moved. Never afraid. Occasional dry humor that surprises people.

> *"Romans name everything they find. That is how they believe they own it."*

> *"I have been dying from a sickness for two years. I fight anyway. Your spear will not frighten me."*

> *"Your fort smells of fear. My camp smells of wood smoke. Fear is the worse smell."*

### Vercingetorix: What He Knows

Vercingetorix carries three generations of knowledge about the spear. He will not volunteer this. He shares it in pieces, based on how much the party earns his respect. Use this table as a guide:

**Social paths to earn his respect (all available, player chooses approach):**

- **Persuasion DC 14** (active: acknowledging his people's legitimate claim on the spear's history): Standard social path. He responds to people who treat Germanic history as real, not as savage tradition.
- **Intimidation DC 14** (active: a controlled display of martial competence rather than a threat -- demonstrating you understand how he fights and that you could have killed him and chose not to): He does not respond to threats. He responds to *audacia*: the kind of courage that is proven, not claimed. A character who fought him directly and performed well can use that as leverage instead of words. This is not menacing him -- it is showing him the kind of soldier he respects. On success, he says: *"You fight well for a Roman. That is the second sentence. The first was everything before."* This immediately moves him to Medium trust.
- **Insight DC 13** (active: reading his body language while he speaks and responding to what he actually needs rather than what he says): He is not negotiating. He is assessing. A character who reads this and responds to the assessment rather than the surface conversation jumps one trust level on their first successful exchange.

| Trust level | What he shares |
|---|---|
| **None** (fought him, ignored him) | Nothing. He says: *"Romans do not earn knowledge. They take it. I will not give you this."* |
| **Low** (treated him as an enemy but stopped fighting) | *"The spear has a name in my language. It means 'the thing that should not exist.' My grandfather helped seal it. He did not think Romans would find it."* |
| **Medium** (talked to him, acknowledged his people's claim) | The above, plus: *"It cannot be destroyed by Roman hands alone. There is a place. A grove. One day's march into the Teutoburg Forest, past the Vitulans river. My people know the way. You do not."* |
| **High** (openly respected his people, treated him as an equal) | All of the above, plus: *"The grove requires a willing sacrifice. Not blood. Something real. My grandfather's ritual failed because the Roman soldier who volunteered chose something he did not actually care about. The grove knew."* This is the core ritual mechanic for Session 3, given early. |
| **Complete trust** (proved by action) | *"I am dying. I have perhaps a year. This is my last campaign. I chose this one because of the spear. If your party destroys it, my people's three-generation wound closes. That is enough for me."* This unlocks Vercingetorix as a full ally for Sessions 3 and 4 -- he will go to the grove himself. |

**If the party kills Vercingetorix in Session 2:** His lieutenant (use the same trust track, same knowledge -- the lieutenant carries everything Vercingetorix knew, but the personal history is absent). The Complete Trust entry costs one additional exchange to unlock because the party killed their chief. That is the consequence, not a brick wall. Use Arnulf from the NPC token set, same Gladiator stat block.

**Dying condition detail (DM only):** Vercingetorix is dying from a slow wasting illness -- almost certainly a Roman-introduced fever disease he contracted during trading contact with frontier settlements. His tribe's healers have no remedy. He knows what it is; he has watched it take others. He does not tell the party unless they reach Complete Trust because it changes how they treat him, and he does not want that. In Session 4 "dying faster" means the siege stress is accelerating the wasting. By Session 5's epilogue he has perhaps three months.

### Vercingetorix Extended Dialogue

Beyond the battle scene, he speaks like this across the session:

When offered food: *"I eat what my men eat. You may sit with us if you wish. It is not insult to eat plainly."*

When the Tribune dismisses him: *"That man's father bought his rank. I can tell by how he holds his shoulders. A man who earned his place does not carry himself like borrowed furniture."*

When asked why he raided the fort tonight specifically: *"The god-killer woke. I felt it from my camp. So did every warrior with a spirit-sense in three tribes. You brought it to the surface. It announced itself."*

When someone asks if he fears Rome: *"No. I have met Romans who were worth fearing. You might be among them. I have not decided."*

### Varro Contingency

If Varro is killed during the raid:

The party loses their most reliable ally inside the fort and the primary witness who can speak to the Tribune's suspicious behaviour. Adjust as follows:

- The Tribune's false accusation in Scene 4 is significantly harder to refute (Varro was the one who would have contradicted him). Add +3 to the Persuasion DC for any negotiation option in Scene 4.
- Cassia takes on some of Varro's role: she can verify the Tribune's inaction during the raid (she was watching from the shrine).
- Three legionaries who served under Varro for more than five years will step forward to defend the party without orders, citing Varro's standing orders: *"He told us: if something happens to him, trust the party. His words."* This gives the party a moment of loyalty they didn't expect.
- Varro's personal effects are looted from his quarters by the Tribune's men within the hour. Inside his locked dispatch box (DC 14 Thieves' Tools to pick): a letter to his wife and a brief note to the party: *"If you're reading this without me, the Tribune moved faster than I expected. Don't trust the Legate either. Trust yourselves. -- V"*

### Session 2 to Session 3 Transition

Whatever ends Session 2, Session 3 begins from a specific position. Confirm which ending applies and use the matching opening.

| Session 2 ending | Session 3 opening |
|---|---|
| **Tribune exposed, arrested** | Party is free but politically exposed. The Legate is temporarily back in command and not grateful. Session 3 begins with them leaving the fort under their own terms -- but Rome now knows their names. |
| **Party fought the Praetorians** | They're fugitives. Session 3 begins 12 hours later, in the forest. They left fast with what they could carry. Vercingetorix found them at the treeline. |
| **Negotiated a deal with the Tribune** | Uneasy alliance. Session 3 begins with the Tribune traveling with the party -- unwillingly, but cooperating. He's useful and he knows it and he's not happy about it. |
| **Fled with Vercingetorix** | Session 3 begins in his camp, two miles north. They're Roman soldiers in a Germanic war camp. They're safe only because he said so. |
| **Surrendered (party gave up the spear)** | Session 3 begins with them as prisoners being escorted to Rome by Praetorian Guard. The spear is in a sealed crate on a wagon ahead of them. The road to Rome takes six days. |

### Pacing

This session runs hot from the start -- the dead sentry, the Tribune's authority disruption, and the raid should feel like one continuous cascade with no breathing room. That's the pressure cooker. The decision at the end is the first moment of genuine stillness. Use it.

### Role Events This Session

**Frumentarius Senior Advancement trigger.**
Quintus Flavius is the sleeper agent inside the fort. If the party identifies him and either captures him before he escapes or produces definitive proof of his identity to Varro, the *Frumentarius* player has completed the intelligence task that defines the Senior tier: exposing a named enemy asset embedded in friendly forces. Award Senior *Frumentarius* status immediately. If Flavius escapes identified but uncaptured, the trigger is not met: he is named and burned, but still free. He will surface in Session 4 as a potential contact the *Frumentarius* can still turn.

**Sextus: vacancy note.**
Sextus held no named role in the unit roster. His death is a murder mystery hook, not a vacancy event. However, if a player's character occupied a gate-adjacent duty role (any role with perimeter or patrol duties), the murder directly affects their domain. Use that as a roleplay pressure: someone died doing a job that character owns.

### Commendationes This Session

**Opportunity 1: protecting the fort during the raid with demonstrable leadership.**
Any character who directly coordinates the defense (rallies soldiers, holds a specific position under pressure, saves a sector that was about to break) earns one *commendatio* from Corvinus after the session. He gives these grudgingly and will not explain his reasoning. The paperwork is filed correctly regardless.

**Opportunity 2: exposing the Tribune's false accusation through evidence, not personal appeal.**
The Tribune accuses the party of treason. Refuting it with physical evidence (the decoded letter, the boot print, Clue 3) rather than argument demonstrates exactly the kind of institutional reliability that formal commendations recognize. One *commendatio* to the character who produces the decisive piece of evidence. If no evidence is produced and the party argues their way out instead, no *commendatio* is awarded this session for that action.

**Opportunity 3: treating Vercingetorix as a legitimate party in negotiation.**
Not a standard Roman military *commendatio*. But if the party reaches Complete Trust with Vercingetorix, he does something at the session end that will surface in Session 3: he sends a runner to Corvinus the following morning with a single message. The message says nothing useful. Its purpose is to establish that the party's word is good with his people. This is not a *commendatio*; it is a different kind of record, and it matters.

### Corruption Tracking

If any character attuned to or touched the spear in Session 1, they get dreams again. Before Scene 3, the player with the highest corruption level describes their dream to the table — the spear shows them the fort burning, their comrades dead, and themselves standing over the ruins holding it. They wake covered in sweat. Don't make this mechanical yet; just make it felt.


### Skill Audit: Session 2

**How to run these checks at the table:**

*Nature DC 11 (passive -- character with +1 or better Nature, if on night watch before the raid):*

The birds near the treeline went silent two hours before the attack. A coordinated force moving slowly through undergrowth does this consistently. Give the player the observation directly: something large and organized was moving into position well before the raid began. This was not a response to the Tribune's arrival -- it was planned in advance.

*Religion DC 13 (passive -- character with +3 or better Religion, during the Tribune's formal arrival speech):*

He skips the traditional ward gesture. A character with this passive knows the invocation he uses requires the gesture to be complete; without it the oath is technically unsworn. He either does not know the form, or he chose not to bind himself. Neither answer is reassuring.

*Arcana DC 13 (passive -- character with +3 or better Arcana, examining the ROMA CADIT carving):*

The letter strokes are angular and deliberate -- the same runic carving technique used on the spear. Roman cursive uses rounded forms. These strokes are not Roman. Whoever made this had exposure to Germanic inscriptional practice. That is not a standard skill for a Roman sleeper agent. Someone taught him.

*Medicine DC 13 (active: examining Sextus' body):*
- Land 5 below: Short blade, from behind. One stroke. That is all they can say.
- Exact: The weapon was a Roman legionary dagger. The angle is consistent with someone shorter, or someone kneeling. This was practiced, not panicked.
- 5 above: He had already drawn his own blade. He had time to react and did not. He knew the attacker, or something he was watching mattered more. Give the player this observation and let them hold it.

*Survival DC 12 (active: reading the ground around the carving before looking at the message):*

The approach path is readable in the mud: the carver came from inside the fort, not from the gate, and left toward the stables. The boot print is confirmation of what Survival already told them. Running both checks (Survival then Investigation) gives the complete picture: where they came from, where they went, and what they look like when they walk.

*Investigation DC 14 (active: examining the ROMA CADIT carving closely):*
- Land 5 below: Latin, recent, last 12 hours.
- Exact: Practiced hand, written fast, listening for something while carving. Not a message for the party. A cover.
- 5 above: The tool marks match a specific military chisel type. The Faber Decimus has three. One came back this morning with a chipped edge. Write "chipped edge" in your notes: this pays off when they look at Decimus.

*Stealth DC 13 (active: approaching Tribune's quarters past the Praetorian guard) or Deception DC 14 (active: claiming authorization for a security inventory):*

Two different routes into the room. Stealth: get past the guard without being seen -- success means undetected entry, failure means a confrontation and the guard reports it to the Tribune within the hour. Deception: claim official authority -- success buys 10 minutes unattended in the room; failure means the guard is now watching them specifically for the rest of the session.

*Investigation DC 16 (active: searching Tribune's quarters thoroughly) or Thieves' Tools DC 14 (active: picking the lock on the dispatch box):*

Investigation finds the box through a careful search; Thieves' Tools opens it directly. A character can attempt both. Finding the box without opening it is still a clue -- the box exists, it is locked, and the Tribune locked it.

*Perception DC 14 / Insight DC 14 (active: watching the Tribune specifically during the raid alarm):*

Both skills reach the same information by different paths. Perception notices the physical fact -- he moves toward the principia, not the walls, and his Praetorians follow without being ordered to. Insight reads his face during the alarm: not fear of raiders, something else. Something like relief that an event has begun on schedule. Either check gives Clue 2.

*History DC 13 (passive -- character with +3 or better History):*

"G.C.B." is enough for a character with Roman political history. Gaius Cassius Brutus is documented: Republican rhetoric, frontier contracts, known for funding causes that weaken the Emperor's frontier authority. A character who passes this knows why destroying a divine weapon found on the frontier serves Brutus' interests -- it removes something the Emperor could use.

::: {.dm-note}
**DM note -- the compound name:** Players with classical history knowledge will notice that "Gaius Cassius Brutus" combines two of the most famous Republican assassins: Gaius Cassius Longinus and Marcus Junius Brutus. They are right to notice it. Brutus chose this cognomen deliberately -- he is not descended from either figure. He adopted the compound name as a political statement, aligning himself with the tradition of senatorial checks on military power. If players ask about it, confirm their suspicion: this is his manifesto written in his name. He sees himself as heir to that tradition, not a murderer, but a corrector of tyrants.
:::


*Insight DC 16 (active: reading the Tribune during a sustained conversation):*
- Land 5 below: He is performing. You can see that much. What is underneath it: not visible yet.
- Exact: Anxiety, not confidence. The performance is good but it is covering something.
- 5 above: He is reading from a script. He has been told what to say. He hesitates before the fourth and seventh statements -- the ones furthest from what he actually believes. Give the player those two specific moments by name.

*Persuasion DC 17 (active: pressing the Tribune directly with evidence in hand):*

He drops the act -- slightly. Not because he trusts the party, but because maintaining the performance under direct confrontation with evidence costs him more than a partial admission. The partial admission is still a tactical retreat, not an honest moment. Watch for the difference.

*Athletics DC 12 (active: pushing back a scaling ladder with raiders on it):*

Two characters pushing the same ladder halve the effective resistance. A miss by 3 or less means the ladder holds but slips -- they have one more round before it locks in place.

*Acrobatics DC 11 (active: reaching the ballista platform via a non-standard route when the main approach is blocked):*

During a wall defense, standard routes clog fast. A character who opts for the fast route instead of the clear route rolls Acrobatics. Success: they reach the ballista one round faster. Failure: they reach it, but spent a bonus action recovering their footing.

*Performance DC 13 (active: delivering a battle speech before the wall holds or breaks):*

Same DC as Persuasion and Intimidation for the wall defense. Different approach: soldiers respond to emotion here as much as authority. A character who performs rather than orders gets a different reaction -- the soldiers don't obey because they have to; they hold because they want to. That distinction matters if the wall takes damage and the same check needs to be repeated.

**Temporal gate: Tribune's doubt (Scene 3 only):**

One round. One check per player. This check only exists while the Tribune is delivering his false accusation in Scene 3.

- *Insight DC 14 (active: watching his face during the accusation, window closes when he finishes speaking):* He hesitates before "enemies of Rome." Half a second. His eyes move to Varro (or Varro's absence) before he continues. He has been given lines and is not fully committed to them.
- *What it opens:* Negotiation DC in Scene 4 drops from 17 to 14. The player can invoke the hesitation directly: "You paused. You know this isn't true."
- *Why the window closes:* Once he finishes the accusation and leaves, he has committed. The doubt sealed over the moment he completed the speech. Catching him before he finishes is catching him before the choice became a fact.

<details>
<summary>**Cascade unlock: soldier at the wall (Scene 2 battle)** *(DM only)*</summary>

This check has an upgrade path. Run it both ways (Persuasion, Intimidation, or Performance, same DC):

- *DC 13 exact:* Soldiers hold. That is the job done.
- *DC 17 (any of the three social skills):* Soldiers hold AND note a name: Flavus, 19 years old, first posting, the one who was about to break. He remembers who held the wall for him. Write his name in your session record now. He appears in Session 4 as an escort volunteer. He does not need to be recruited: he recruits himself.

</details>
